f: What does a dashed asymptote line show on a graph?
b: A boundary line (rose role [[k|k]]) that the curve approaches closely but never crosses.

f: What is the role of the shaded area under f(x)?
b: It shows the accumulated total (integral) over an interval, matching the teal group role [[g|g]].

f: In a bias-variance graph, what happens in the overfitting zone?
b: Training error keeps dropping, but validation error rises because the model memorizes noise.

f: How does the Differences filter help on a comparison table?
b: It dims rows where all options behave identically so only the real trade-offs stand out.

f: In a branching flowchart, what do green vs. rose edge pills signal?
b: Green ([[Yes|r]]) marks the pass/accepted branch; rose ([[No|k]]) marks the fallback or error branch.

f: Why does an API architecture diagram separate the Cache from the Database?
b: The cache serves repeated reads in milliseconds, shielding the slower persistent database from excess load.

f: Why is model training drawn as a cycle instead of a one-way line?
b: Each pass measures prediction loss and updates weights, looping until error settles.

f: What does the filled progress line on a timeline indicate?
b: Which milestones have already occurred up to the active step, separating past context from future events.

f: In an ID3 decision tree, what does the root node represent?
b: The attribute with the highest Information Gain—the split that removes the most uncertainty first.

f: What does a leaf node do in a decision tree?
b: It ends the branch and outputs a concrete decision or class label (green result role).

f: When does Alpha-Beta pruning cut a branch in a Minimax tree?
b: When the current move already guarantees a worse outcome than a sibling option found earlier (\beta \le \alpha).

f: Why use semantic color roles across equations, graphs, trees, and tables?
b: The same color means the same thing everywhere in a section, so your eye connects the formula to the picture.

f: How do synthesized and inherited arrows differ on an SDD parse tree?
b: Green synthesized arrows carry values bottom-up from children; dashed amber inherited arrows pass left/parent context down or sideways.

f: What does a double halo on a Kit.dag node signal?
b: A shared/merge node with 2 or more incoming parents—computed once and reused without duplicating work.
